title: Protesters march in Besançon against cost of living
seoTitle: Besançon march against cost of living

tea.why: Participants demonstrated against the rising cost of living, marking the eighth anniversary of the yellow vest movement.
tea.want: Protesters demanded relief from high living costs and expressed frustration with the political situation.
tea.changed: Nov 21: Police reported six arrests following clashes and property damage at the end of the march in Besançon.

summary: On November 21, 2026, an undeclared demonstration took place in Besançon against the rising cost of living, coinciding with the eighth anniversary of the yellow vest movement. According to news reports, approximately 1,600 to 2,000 people gathered at the Parc des Glacis before marching through the streets. Because authorities had issued a ban on entering the city center, police forces blocked access routes, prompting the procession to redirect toward the Belfort street area. The demonstration concluded around 18:00 amid heightened tensions, clashes with police, and bin fires. According to the prefecture, security forces carried out six arrests and reported damage to a bank storefront in the Chaprais sector.
response: According to the prefecture, the protest was not declared and city center access was banned by decree. Police deployed tear gas during clashes, and authorities reported six arrests alongside damage to a bank storefront.

updates.text: An undeclared protest against the cost of living starts at Parc des Glacis in Besançon with around 2,000 participants.
Police block access to the city center due to a prefectural ban, redirecting the procession toward Belfort street.
The demonstration ends with clashes, tear gas, bin fires, and six arrests reported by the prefecture.
